name: Health and pharmaceuticals
summary: Ethiopia's local pharmaceutical industry is scaling up quickly: the government says local suppliers now cover more than 44 percent of national procurement of drugs and medical equipment, up from about 8 percent five or six years earlier, and it aims to raise the share of locally produced medicines and medical supplies above 50 percent by 2030. The World Bank reports that the national regulator has reached WHO Maturity Level 3, opening new export opportunities, and that the dedicated Kilinto pharmaceutical zone already hosts nearly 30 investors, supported by tax holidays and price preferences for domestic manufacturers. In services, the Ethiopian Investment Commission points to strong demand for hospital capacity, with only 17% of tertiary hospitals private and more than $120 million a year spent by Ethiopians on treatment abroad.

opportunities.title: Kilinto pharmaceutical zone
opportunities.detail: The Kilinto Special Economic Zone covers 279 hectares (160 hectares leasable) and serves as a dedicated hub for pharmaceutical and medical equipment manufacturing; nearly 30 investors are present, at stages ranging from construction to active production.

opportunities.title: Finished drugs, vaccines and biologics
opportunities.detail: The Ethiopian Investment Commission lists finished dose forms, antisera, vaccines, toxins, cultures and glandular extracts as manufacturing opportunities, citing demand growth of an average of 15% over the past five years.

opportunities.title: Tertiary and specialty hospitals
opportunities.detail: The Commission promotes tertiary hospitals with a minimum of 300 beds serving local and inbound patients, to capture part of the more than $120 million Ethiopians spend annually on treatment abroad.

opportunities.title: Advanced diagnostics and laboratories
opportunities.detail: The Commission identifies advanced diagnostics and laboratories offering over 400 tests in Ethiopia, including the production of laboratory reagents, as an investment opportunity.

opportunities.title: Local pharmaceutical inputs
opportunities.detail: An AHRI feasibility study handed to the Ministry of Health found a cassava starch plant of 14,611 tons a year would have about 90% import substitution potential, with opportunities for regional export.

opportunities.title: Equipment and supplies for new facilities
opportunities.detail: The US Commercial Service lists equipment and services for new hospitals and health centers, cold storage, pharmaceutical warehouses and IT support among leading sub-sectors.

incentives.detail: Ethiopia has introduced tax holidays and price preferences of up to 50 percent for eligible domestic manufacturers of medicines and medical supplies (per the Ministry of Health report carried by ENA).
The Ethiopian Pharmaceutical Supply Agency gives local manufacturers 25% price protection when competing with foreign suppliers and a 30% advance payment with long-term agreements.

The national regulator's WHO Maturity Level 3 status, and mutual recognition agreements among ML3 countries, are described by the World Bank as opening new export opportunities for locally made medicines.

risks.detail: Foreign exchange access is a planning factor for importing equipment and supplies, according to the US Commercial Service; investors should build import timing and currency needs into project plans.

Buyers are price-sensitive and the imported medical equipment and supplies market is led by Chinese suppliers; public tenders can involve lengthy bidding procedures. Local manufacturers can draw on the price preferences and EPSA price protection listed under incentives.

Commodity price movements can affect input costs; under the IMF-supported reform program, which reached staff-level agreement on its fifth review in June 2026, the IMF encourages further improvement in the functioning and transparency of the foreign exchange market.
